sovereign_country.strategic_role: 西欧核心消费市场、高客单价品牌合规与本土清关

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Cross-Border Reverse Logistics and Returned Goods Quality Grading

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Code monétaire et financier (Articles L561-1 et seq.) and Ordonnance n° 2017-1164 du 12 septembre 2017 relative à la transparence de la vie économique et des procédures de lutte contre les corruptions et la fraude
ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening against PEP lists, OFAC SDN, UN Sanctions, and French Tracfin database

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: French language using Latin script; no transliteration required
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Words implying public authority without authorization
Names confusingly similar to existing entities
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Administrative appeal to the Minister of the Economy and Finance or judicial appeal to the Tribunal de Commerce within 2 months of rejection

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Accepted for registered office address in France for administrative and tax purposes
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low risk of unannounced physical inspections; routine checks during tax audits or licensing

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Legal due diligence and incorporation services
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for French corporate formation
Prevailing market rate for Hague Apostille

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce), Articles L.227-1 to L.227-44 (SAS); L.210-1 to L.210-10 (general company law); L.210-6 (legal personality from registration); associated R.123 registry filing provisions.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Guichet unique operated by the Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle (INPI), transmitted to the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce for registration in the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Association (Statuts) and the standard RCS incorporation dossier (online M0 form via the formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr one-stop portal).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: The SAS has no legislated minimum share capital. The Statuts must fix a capital that is fully subscribed at incorporation. For cash contributions, at least 50% of the nominal amount must be paid up on subscription; the remaining amount may be called within five years. Paid-up cash contributions must be evidenced by a bank deposit certificate or notary sequestration until registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED by the sole shareholder, exercising in accordance with Article L.227-1 of the French Commercial Code, that: (1) the Statuts are adopted and the entire stated share capital is subscribed and paid up as required; (2) the registered office is fixed at [address], within the competence of [commercial court]; (3) [name] is appointed President for the duration of the company, vested with all powers to represent the SAS, open bank accounts, execute contracts, and complete all registration, tax and social filings. The President is authorized to take every administrative step and to delegate routine powers to a legal representative.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the Statuts and Founding Governance Pack
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Private execution by the initial shareholder(s); optional notarization by a French notaire if real-property contributions are made.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Statuts in French setting out the SAS name, duration, share capital, number and nominal value of shares, exact corporate object covering cross-border reverse logistics, returned-goods quality grading and transport coordination, registered office, management powers, and share transfer restrictions. Have all shareholders initial every page, sign the final pages and date the instrument. If cash contributions are made, prepare the corresponding payment instructions. No statutory audit of contributions is required if the contribution consists solely of cash.
required_dossiers: Proof of individual share subscription amounts
Capital payment instruction or deposit instruction
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the shareholders or the notary identify a defect, execute a supplemental rectification agreement and re-initial the affected pages before filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication of the Legal Notice of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: An authorized legal journal (Journal d'annonces légales) in the department of the registered office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Place a legal notice in an approved legal gazette before filing the RCS dossier. The notice must state the corporate name, legal form, share capital, registered office, corporate object, duration, President's details and the composition of the statutory management. Obtain the publisher's attestation of publication (attestation de parution) to attach to the registration file.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the legal journal demands clarifications or rejects the notice, correct the text and republish; the corrected attestation replaces the earlier version in the RCS file.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Deposit of Share Capital and Obtaining the Deposit Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: French commercial bank or a notary office acting as sequestrator.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a non-withdrawable blocked account in the name of the company in formation and deposit the paid-up cash contributions. Obtain a certificate of deposit from the bank or notary evidencing the funds. The certificate must be dated within the statutory period before filing. After the SAS is registered, the President withdraws the funds by presenting the Kbis extract.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank delays KYC approval, engage a notary as sequestrator to hold the funds and issue the required certificate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission of the Formation Dossier to the INPI Guichet Unique
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr; file forwarded to the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce of the registered office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the online RCS incorporation form indicating legal form SAS and the primary French APE/NAF activity corresponding to ISIC 5229 (typically 52.29B). Upload the signed Statuts, legal publication certificate, bank deposit certificate, proof of registered office address, identity documents, and the President's declaration on honour of non-conviction. Sign electronically, pay the applicable registry fee and track the dossier until the Registry issues the Kbis extract. The SAS obtains legal personality upon RCS registration.
required_dossiers: Attestation de parution du journal d'annonces légales
Proof of address of registered office
Déclaration sur l'honneur de non-conviction du président
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry issues a query, submit the requested rectification within the 15-day statutory response period; an amended Statuts and corrected supporting document may be uploaded without restarting the process.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INSEE (Sirene), Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce, URSSAF, DGFIP.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After issuance of the Kbis, retrieve the SIRET number and verify the APE code. If the SAS will employ staff, complete employer registration with URSSAF and activate payroll declarations. Obtain a VAT number from DGFIP for cross-border operations. Open the company's operating bank account and, if desired, activate payment rails such as Local ACH or Airwallex using the Kbis and President's mandate.
required_dossiers: URSSAF employer registration forms (if employees are hired)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If INSEE assigns an incorrect APE code, file a correction request through the Sirene portal; if URSSAF account creation is delayed, contact the URSSAF regional office with the SIRET and President's identity to trigger manual issuance.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Direction régionale de l'économie, de l'emploi, du travail et des solidarités (DREETS) and Direction régionale de l'environnement, de l'aménagement et du logement (DREAL), acting for the préfet under the ICPE regime.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No France-specific operating licence is required for returned-goods reverse logistics and quality grading; the RCS/SIRET registration and, where the physical site exceeds environmental thresholds, an ICPE declaration or registration constitute the operating clearances.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: DREAL / Préfecture de département, under the French Code de l'environnement and the ICPE regime.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt from a full EIA for a pure returns-sorting and reverse-logistics facility; however, a simple declaration or registration may be mandatory under ICPE rubric 1510 where covered warehouse storage surfaces or volumes exceed the applicable regulatory thresholds.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial wastewater, VOC process emissions or combustion furnace is anticipated. Sanitary and rainwater discharges must comply with local sewer bylaws and water authority permits; any pre-treatment agreement will impose COD/BOD5/TSS thresholds and pH limits (generally 6.5–8.5, temperature below 30°C). Non-road mobile machinery must comply with EU Stage V emission standards; returned electrical or electronic waste must be handled or registered under the applicable EPR and waste-shipment rules.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Workplace fire-safety certification covering fire extinguishers, emergency exits, alarm systems and electrical installations; structural load verification for racking or mezzanines; occupational health-and-safety checklist under the French Labour Code, including prevention of musculoskeletal risks and access for disabled persons where the premises are open to staff or third parties.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction générale des Finances publiques (DGFiP). The principal online portal is impots.gouv.fr; foreign businesses generally deal with the Service des impôts des entreprises étrangères (SIEE) for French tax registration and VAT matters.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A French SAS is registered through the applicable company-formation formalities and receives a SIREN and SIRET from the national business-registration system; it must then complete tax formalities with the DGFiP and obtain a French VAT identification number where required. A foreign entity making taxable supplies in France should apply to the SIEE for VAT registration before commencing those supplies, providing evidence of legal existence, constitutional documents, business activities, identity and authority of representatives, and details of French taxable transactions. A non-EU-established business generally must appoint a French fiscal representative unless an applicable mutual-assistance arrangement or statutory exception removes that requirement. EU-established businesses generally do not require such a representative. A VAT number does not itself establish a permanent establishment or determine corporate-tax residence.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: A French SAS is generally subject to French corporate income tax (impôt sur les sociétés, IS). Eligible qualifying small companies may elect temporarily for taxation under the personal income-tax regime, subject to statutory conditions, shareholder and activity tests, and a limited election period. This is not a US-style check-the-box election. France has no general domestic check-the-box mechanism for classifying foreign entities; foreign-entity treatment follows French tax-law characterization and applicable treaty rules. Hybrid mismatch rules may deny deductions or require inclusion under applicable French and EU anti-hybrid legislation.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT, taxe sur la valeur ajoutée or TVA), harmonized under the EU VAT system
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 85,000 annual domestic turnover for supplies of goods and certain comparable activities, and EUR 37,500 for services under the domestic small-business VAT exemption thresholds, subject to statutory conditions and applicable tolerance thresholds. These thresholds generally do not protect a non-established business making taxable supplies in France: registration and VAT accounting may be required from the first taxable transaction. Special EU cross-border SME arrangements and transaction-specific rules may apply.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: France does not generally operate real-time VAT invoice clearance or mandatory digital stamping. Domestic B2B e-invoicing is being phased in: from 1 September 2026, all businesses must be able to receive compliant electronic invoices, while large and intermediate-sized businesses must issue them; SMEs and micro-enterprises are scheduled to issue from 1 September 2027. In-scope invoices must use an authorized platform and compliant formats. E-reporting applies to specified transactions, including relevant B2C and cross-border transactions, under the phased implementation timetable. Foreign businesses should verify whether their French transactions fall within the domestic mandate.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods from France to a destination outside the EU may be exempt with deduction (effectively 0% VAT) where the supplier establishes that the goods were dispatched or transported outside the EU and satisfies documentary and invoicing requirements. Intra-EU supplies are governed by separate rules and generally require dispatch to another Member State, a valid customer VAT identification number, and supporting evidence. Services are not automatically zero-rated as exports: place-of-supply rules generally determine treatment, with B2B services commonly taxed where the business customer is established and statutory exceptions applying. Returned-goods logistics require transaction-specific analysis; a return or re-export does not by itself establish eligibility for export exemption or import relief.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: French/EU export customs declaration and customs-office export certification or equivalent electronic exit confirmation
Commercial invoice, packing list, and records identifying the goods and linking the shipment to the sale or return transaction
Transport evidence, such as a bill of lading, air waybill, CMR consignment note, or carrier delivery and exit records
Customer order, contract, return authorization, and warehouse or inventory records supporting the goods' movement and ownership
Banking or payment records where relevant to substantiate the transaction; an Inward Remittance Certificate is not a generally prescribed French export-VAT document
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: France imposes no general statutory foreign-exchange repatriation deadline for export proceeds. The zero value above denotes that no 180-day or other general deadline applies, not a required repatriation period. Unsupported or false export exemption claims may result in reassessment of VAT, late-payment interest, and tax penalties; penalties depend on the nature, amount, and intent of the breach and may be higher for deliberate or fraudulent conduct. Input VAT deductions and refunds may also be denied or recovered. Customs and tax records should be retained under applicable French statutory requirements and produced on audit.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (Bank of France) is the central monetary and exchange-control authority; statistical surveillance of cross-border capital movements is administered jointly with the Direction Générale du Trésor (French Treasury) under the Code monétaire et financier and Articles 63–66 TFEU (free movement of capital).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France grants full legal convertibility for current and capital transactions; the EUR is freely transferable and no prior central-bank approval applies to equity subscriptions, dividend remittances, or liquidation proceeds. The French foreign-investment screening regime (Decree No. 2019-1590, Articles L151-3 et seq. CMF) covers only strategic sectors, and ISIC 5229 reverse logistics is outside the sensitive list, so no prior investment authorisation is required. Practical profit-remittance hurdles are documentary: positive distributable reserves, a valid corporate distribution resolution, FATCA/CRS self-certification, and the applicable non-resident dividend withholding tax (25–30%) unless reduced by tax treaty or exempted under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive (parent holding ≥10% for at least 24 months).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: France has no mandatory export-proceeds surrender or conversion ratio; foreign-currency receivables may be retained in onshore devisen-denominated accounts without central-bank instruction. Statutory reporting alone binds the operator: any resident entity with aggregate cross-border transfers (receipts and payments) of at least EUR 750,000 in a calendar month must electronically declare them to the Banque de France through the MERIDIA channel within 20 business days after month-end (Articles L.141-1 to L.165-2 CMF). Returned-merchandise reversal flows collected from foreign merchants are coded as services or re-export flows for balance-of-payments statistics; no forced conversion applies to such receipts.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (compte de dépôt professionnel) / Capital Escrow Account (compte séquestre)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: High feasibility as an ancillary payment and wiring rail, Medium as the sole treasury custodian. Airwallex (expressly targeted as a payment rail) operates under an EU electronic-money institution licence (Bank of Lithuania as home supervisor), passported into France under PSD2/EMD2 and supervised by the ACPR for payment services; it offers multi-currency SWIFT, SEPA and Local ACH rails with segregated client funds and competitive FX pricing. Legal constraints: an EMI is not a French credit institution and cannot provide a regulated capital escrow (compte séquestre), payroll/VAT-linked settlement with full banking liability, overdraft facilities, or treasury credit; French tax practice requires the payroll/VAT account to be held at an ACPR-licensed credit institution. Optimal architecture: Airwallex for cross-border supplier, merchant and refund payments, and a tier-1 French bank for statutory escrow, share-capital and tax settlement accounts.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Mandatory in practice. Article R561-5 CMF (implementation of the 4AMLD/5AMLD framework) requires the bank to identify the legal entity and its natural-person directors and UBOs holding 25% or more of capital. French clearing banks accept remote opening only where an ANSSI/eIDAS-qualified electronic identification solution and verification anchors (micro-credit, account-holding confirmation) are used; in practice, for a newly incorporated SAS with non-resident shareholders, the tier-1 banks require a physical appointment at a French branch of the managing director (Président / Directeur Général) and typically of the UBO(s). Original K-bis registration extract, RBE extract, passports, proof of address dated under three months, articles of association and the bank's corporate KYC questionnaire must be produced. A notarised power of attorney with apostille to a locally resident treasury manager who appears in person is the only widely accepted substitute; remote video-only interviews are rarely honoured by the major French banks.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opacity of non-resident ultimate beneficial ownership (UBO chain through foreign holding vehicles or trusts)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Current RBE extract (déclaration des bénéficiaires effectifs), certified corporate ownership and tracing chart, passport copies and three-month proof of address of each natural-person UBO, statutory declaration that no nominee/fiduciary arrangement exists, and, if a trust or fund sits in the chain, the trust deed, register of beneficiaries and the reporting required by Article 1649-AB CGI.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions or integrity screening hits (OFAC, EU restrictive measures, Russian/Ukrainian sanctions lists) on a non-resident director or shareholder with a common name
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full identity set (passport, national identity card), utility bills covering the last six months, a certified sanctions-screening report from a recognised data provider (World-Check/Refinitiv), an explanatory letter, and confirmation that neither the beneficial owners nor the transaction counterparties are designated persons, enabling the bank's compliance committee to close the false-positive match.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source-of-funds opacity for an inbound equity injection aggregating EUR 750,000 or more in one calendar month
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Six months of bank statements of the remitting shareholder, the board-approved or notarised capital-subscription resolution, proof of the upstream liquidation event (if the shareholder is a holding vehicle), the investor's certificate of tax residence, and the Banque de France MERIDIA balance-of-payments declaration receipt evidencing that the transfer was reported.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Perceived high-risk activity: reverse logistics of returned merchandise possibly associated with counterfeit goods, stolen inventory or IP infringement
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Brand-authorised reverse-logistics agreements (marketplace and merchant contracts), the SAS's EORI and French customs registrations, VAT registration certificate, RMA traceability workflow, anti-counterfeiting and goods-disposal SOPs, insurance certificates, K-bis description confirming ISIC 5229, and brand licenses covering quality grading and refurbishment.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: PEP status or inconsistent tax domiciliation of a non-resident manager or beneficial owner
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed PEP self-declaration of each manager and UBO, French tax-residence certificate (attestation de résidence fiscale) or Article 1975-A CGI certificate, evidence of substance in France (registered office, lease, payroll/URSSAF account, operational warehouse), and proof of genuine economic activity reconciling the manager's tax residency with the SAS's management seat.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity requires no FX authorisation: the non-resident shareholder transmits EUR via SWIFT MT103/MT202 (TARGET2 euro clearing) to the SAS's euro account at a French tier-1 bank. The bank will credit the funds as share capital only after verifying the share-subscription resolution, updated articles and K-bis, RBE extract and remitter identity; funds intended as equity must not be routed as shareholder current-account flows. The SAS must file the Banque de France balance-of-payments declaration via MERIDIA when the aggregate monthly external flow equals or exceeds EUR 750,000, using the inward-direct-investment transaction code and the ISIC 5229 activity tag; the wire's remittance-information field should reference 'CAPITAL_SUBSCRIPTION_FR_SAS_ISIC5229_[DATE]_[EUR]' and the remitter's LEI.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Treasury clearing stack by counterparty geography: (1) intra-EEA suppliers, merchants and carriers settle via SEPA Credit Transfer or SEPA Instant on the EPC clearing perimeter, using the French IBAN with structured remittance references (invoice and RMA number); (2) non-EEA and non-EUR payments (United Kingdom, Hong Kong, United States, China) settle via SWIFT MT103 (gpi with UETR) through the French correspondent-banking network for freight, grading fees and merchant refunds; (3) large-scale re-export of graded returned goods settles under commercial letters of credit (UCP 600) or documentary collections (URC 522) with inspection certificates and customs declarations (EXA/Intrastat). Every outward transaction must be supported by a commercial invoice bearing the ISIC 5229 service description and must be included in the monthly Banque de France declaration where the EUR 750,000 aggregate threshold is breached; goods flows are captured in Intrastat declarations. Consumer refunds are executed exclusively through SEPA mandates with reverse-logistics refund reference numbers, never via cash or bearer instruments.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable foreign-exchange forward contracts (change à terme) in EUR/USD, EUR/GBP and EUR/CNH provided by French credit institutions under the FBF/ISDA master agreement; no product-level authorisation is required, but EMIR margin rules apply to non-financial counterparties above the relevant clearing thresholds.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDF) as permitted overlays for restricted or illiquid currencies (e.g., CNY, INR) where onshore physical delivery is unavailable; the NDF is cash-settled in EUR and may hedge reverse-logistics collection and refund flows only where matched to an identifiable cross-border settlement exposure.

Cross-currency swaps (EUR/USD and EUR/CNH) aligning external treasury exposures (capital injection, long-term receivables, repatriation programmes) to EUR liabilities; permitted with tier-1 EU banks under the ISDA/FBF protocol, with variation margin collateralised where the aggregate notional exceeds EMIR thresholds; physically settled FX swaps are excluded from the EMIR clearing obligation.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax annual return (déclaration de résultats, form 2065-SD and annexes)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) via the online tax filing portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For calendar-year fiscal year-ends, file and pay the final balance by 3 May or the second business day after 1 May; for off-calendar fiscal years, file within three months of fiscal year-end.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-payment interest accrues at 0.40% per month on unpaid tax; automatic late-filing penalty of 5% of tax due, increased to 10% if filed after formal demand; intentional concealment may attract 40% or 80% penalties.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual financial statements filing (dépôt des comptes annuels, annexes, management report and audit report)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (Registrar of the Commercial Court) through the Guichet unique formalities platform
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months of the fiscal year-end and after shareholder approval of the financial statements.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Any interested person may petition the commercial court for a coercive order to deposit accounts under a daily fine (astreinte); persistent omission for two fiscal years exposes the company to administrative strike-off and director liability for damages.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial ownership declaration update (déclaration des bénéficiaires effectifs) where shareholdings change during the year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registre National des Entreprises (RNE) / Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce via the single filing portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days after any direct or indirect acquisition of 25% or more of share capital or voting rights, or any change in effective control; no separate annual filing is due if ownership is unchanged.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to update may expose the legal representative to a criminal fine of up to €7,500 and imprisonment for intentional omission; the company may also receive an administrative injunction with daily fines.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Quarterly corporate income tax instalments and final annual balance payment (acomptes d'IS and solde de l'IS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Calendar-year companies: instalments due on 15 March, 15 June, 15 September and 15 December; final balance due by 3 May of the following year or the second business day after 1 May.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late instalments accrue monthly late interest of 0.40% plus a 5% penalty; repeated defaults may result in forfeiture of scheduled payment terms and immediate tax enforcement.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A French SAS must appoint a statutory auditor (commissaire aux comptes) if it exceeds at least two of three thresholds at fiscal year-end: total assets over €6.2 million, net turnover excluding tax over €12.2 million, or average permanent headcount over 50. Group-control, listed-entity or public-interest scenarios may require an auditor even below these thresholds.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French GAAP under the Plan Comptable Général (PCG), in accordance with Commercial Code Articles L.123-12 et seq. and EU Directive 2013/34/EU; IFRS is mandatory only for consolidated financial statements of French listed groups.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The French RNE does not impose a standalone annual UBO return for stable ownership. The legal representative must file an updated beneficial-owner declaration within 30 days of becoming aware of any change in the 25% direct or indirect ownership threshold or in effective control. In practice, the annual shareholder approval of accounts is the standard verification point: if the share register reveals an unreported transfer, the single formalities portal must be updated immediately.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (registre des actionnaires et mouvements de titres)
Share Transfer Register (registre des transferts de titres)
Minute Book and corporate decisions (registre des procès-verbaux et décisions sociales)
Register of Directors and Corporate Officers

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: $120–$400 per year for standard domiciliation commerciale, depending on city and service level
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: $3,500–$15,000 per year for a typical small or medium SAS statutory audit, depending on revenue volume, transactions and any group consolidation requirements

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% standard corporate income tax rate for fiscal years beginning on or after 1 January 2022; reduced 15% rate applies to qualifying SMEs on the first €42,500 of taxable profit if turnover < €10 million and capital held >=75% by individuals or qualifying entities.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general tax holiday for SAS. Available incentives include: 15% SME reduced rate; research tax credit (CIR); innovation tax credit (CII); patent box 10% rate for qualifying IP income; young innovative company (JEI) exemptions; urban free zones (ZFU) and rural revitalization zones (ZRR) subject to EU state aid approval; temporary measures for energy costs. Reverse logistics may qualify for CIR if it involves R&D on grading technology.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Indefinite carryforward, subject to annual offset limitation of €1,000,000 plus 50% of taxable profit above €1,000,000; one-year carryback option for qualifying losses.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulaire 2065-SD (Déclaration de résultats) with annexes 2058-A, 2058-B, 2058-C, 2059-A; filed electronically via impots.gouv.fr - Espace professionnel or through an approved EDI partner under the EDI-CIT procedure.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; CIT advance payments (acomptes) are paid quarterly on 15 March, 15 June, 15 September, and 15 December unless an annual option applies.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 3 months of fiscal year-end. For a 31 December year-end, the deadline is the second working day following 1 May of year N+1. Balance of CIT due by 15 May (or the 15th of the fourth month following year-end) for 31 December year-end; advance payments due quarterly.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Bénéfice fiscal (taxable profit) after extra-accounting reclassifications and before loss carryforward.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: French-resident SAS reports worldwide income. Non-resident companies with a French permanent establishment file 2065 for PE-attributable profits and attach 2058-A. Non-residents without a PE generally have no 2065 filing except French-source income subject to withholding tax.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Déficit fiscal (taxable loss) for the fiscal year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: PE losses may be reported; treaty rules on PE loss relief and carryforward apply. Non-residents without a PE cannot claim French CIT losses.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Impôt sur les sociétés at standard rate (25%).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: PE computes CIT on PE profits. Non-resident shareholders do not report here.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Impôt sur les sociétés at reduced 15% SME rate on first €42,500 of profit.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reduced rate generally unavailable to non-resident PE unless qualifying SME conditions are met.
PE aggregates CIT. Treaty non-discrimination may apply.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax credits (crédits d'impôt), including CIR, CII, and foreign tax credits under treaties.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: PE may claim treaty foreign tax credits and French credits attributable to PE.
PE credits quarterly acomptes paid in France.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Balance of CIT payable or refundable credit.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: PE pays balance or claims refund. Non-resident without PE not concerned.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: 10% increase of CIT due (Article 1728 CGI); 40% if not filed within 30 days of formal notice; 80% if concealed activity. Late payment interest: 0.20% per month (Article 1727 CGI). Fixed penalty €150 for failure to file a nil return. Directors jointly liable under Article 1745 CGI.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulaire 2257-SD (Déclaration annuelle des prix de transfert) filed electronically via impots.gouv.fr - Espace professionnel.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Filed simultaneously with the CIT return 2065, within 3 months of fiscal year-end (second working day after 1 May for 31 December year-end).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Name, country, and tax ID of ultimate parent and principal group entities.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: French SAS reports foreign parent details. Foreign parent does not file 2257 unless it has a French PE.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Nature, amount, and counterparties of controlled transactions (services, goods, royalties, interest).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose all transactions between SAS and foreign related parties, including reverse logistics service fees and cost recharges.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Selected OECD method (CUP, resale price, cost plus, TNMM, profit split) and justification.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident parent's TP policy should align; French SAS must document its own functional profile.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Confirmation that Master File and Local File are available within 30 days of tax audit request.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign parent must cooperate to provide group Master File; French SAS retains Local File.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to file 2257-SD: €150,000 fine (Article 223 quinquies B CGI). Failure to provide TP documentation upon audit: €10,000 per fiscal year; €50,000 for failure to respond to formal request within 30 days. Reassessment of profits with 40% penalty for abuse.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 30% standard domestic withholding tax on dividends paid to non-residents (Article 119 bis CGI). EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive exemption applies for EU parent companies holding >=10% of SAS for at least 2 years; treaty rates may reduce to 0-15%.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Beneficiary obtains a valid Tax Residence Certificate (TRC) from its foreign tax authority and provides it to the French payer before payment. Payer applies reduced treaty rate or EU exemption at source, files form 2777-SD, and retains documentation. France requires beneficial ownership, principal purpose test (PPT) analysis, and may request proof of substance. If reduced rate not applied at source, beneficiary files refund claim within 3 years with TRC, proof of ownership, and beneficial owner declaration. Payer may be liable if relief improperly granted.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: statutory withholding tax 33 1/3% (Article 182 B CGI); EU Interest and Royalties Directive exemption for associated EU companies with >=25% shareholding for 2 years; treaty rates typically 0-15%. Interest: statutory withholding tax 30% (Article 125 A CGI); EU Interest and Royalties Directive exemption for qualifying EU associated companies; treaty rates typically 0-15%. Domestic exemptions exist for certain interest paid to EU parents and on listed bonds. Payer must obtain TRC and beneficial ownership documentation.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Master File and Local File mandatory for legal entities or groups with annual turnover or gross assets >= €400 million. Annual transfer pricing declaration (form 2257-SD) mandatory for entities with turnover >= €50 million. Currency: EUR.
